items.title: The complex coordinate map preserves real scalar multiplication
items.statement: The coordinate bijection Φ(a+bi)=(a,b) is real-linear: it preserves addition and satisfies Φ(rz)=rΦ(z) for all r∈R and z∈C, with real scalars embedded canonically.
items.strategy: Write z=a+bi, multiply (r+0i)(a+bi), and apply the coordinate formula; inherit additivity and bijectivity from the coordinate-plane theorem.

sources.title: J. Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis
E. Stein and R. Shakarchi, Complex Analysis, Princeton Lectures in Analysis II

items.title: Polygonal length and rectifiability of complex paths
items.statement: For a continuous γ:[a,b]→C, define polygonal partition sums and their extended-real supremum L_C(γ); γ is rectifiable iff L_C(γ)<+∞. On a singleton interval set L_C=0 and every path is rectifiable.
items.strategy: Give the path and partition conventions explicitly; prove the partition sums are finite nonnegative reals, the supremum is well-defined, and the singleton convention does not invoke a partition.
items.axiom_use: None. Only the ε-δ definition of metric continuity and the extended-real supremum theorem are used; no choice principle is used.

sources.title: E. Stein and R. Shakarchi, Complex Analysis, Princeton Lectures in Analysis II
L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Chapter 4

items.title: The complex coordinate isometry transports topology and affine segments
items.statement: With d_C(z,w)=|z−w| and the Euclidean metric on R², Φ:C→R² is a bijective isometry and homeomorphism, preserves every real affine segment, and transports open/closed sets, interior, closure, boundary, boundedness, compactness, and connectedness for every subset.
items.strategy: Use the exact distance and ball correspondence; derive affine transport from real-linearity; transfer the set properties from their metric definitions and the continuous-image theorems in both directions.
items.axiom_use: None. The compact and connected transports use the supplied continuous-image theorems; this proof uses no choice principle.

sources.title: J. Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis, Section 1.1.1
E. Stein and R. Shakarchi, Complex Analysis, Chapter 1, Section 1.1

items.title: Real total derivatives transport through the complex coordinate isometry
items.statement: For open U⊆C and f:U→C, f_R=Φ∘f∘Φ⁻¹ on Φ[U] is totally differentiable at Φ(z) exactly when f has a real-linear first-order approximation L at z with remainder o(|h|); then Df_R(Φ(z))=Φ∘L∘Φ⁻¹.
items.strategy: Conjugate the candidate real-linear map by Φ and identify the two remainder quotients by the exact isometry; reverse the construction with Φ⁻¹.

sources.title: J. Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis, Section 2.2.2

items.title: Complex path length equals coordinate length and piecewise speed integral
items.statement: For continuous γ:[a,b]→C, each complex polygonal sum equals the Euclidean sum for Γ=Φ∘γ=(x,y); hence L_C(γ)=L_R²(Γ), γ is rectifiable iff x,y have bounded variation, and for continuous piecewise-C¹ Γ its length is the sum of Euclidean speed integrals, including corners and zero-speed pieces.
items.strategy: Use isometry termwise on each partition, take the same supremum, then apply the supplied coordinate-variation and piecewise-speed results; handle singleton intervals separately.

sources.title: L. V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed., Chapter 4, Section 1.2
U. Lang, Differential Geometry I, Section 1.1

items.title: Complex path length is invariant under monotone surjective reparametrization
items.statement: If γ:[a,b]→C is continuous and φ:[c,d]→[a,b] is continuous, surjective, and nondecreasing or nonincreasing, then L_C(γ∘φ)=L_C(γ), including singleton intervals, pauses, and reversal.
items.strategy: Prove γ∘φ is continuous from the metric ε-δ definition, transfer both paths to R², apply the supplied Euclidean reparametrization theorem, and transfer lengths back.
items.axiom_use: None. The local composition-continuity argument uses only ε-δ continuity; the Euclidean theorem uses finite partition choices, not arbitrary choice.

sources.title: E. Stein and R. Shakarchi, Complex Analysis, Chapter 1, Section 3
U. Lang, Differential Geometry I, Section 1.1

title: Complex Coordinate and Path Transport — Examples

items.title: A finite coordinate path and a bounded nonrectifiable path
items.statement: Compute a coordinate, affine, isometry, real-derivative, path-length, pause, reversal, and singleton example; also exhibit a bounded continuous complex path with unbounded polygonal sums.
items.strategy: Direct finite calculations from the A-page interfaces; for the bounded nonrectifiable path, use primitive prefix harmonic sums and prove the doubling-block identity directly by induction on the trailing count, without general lower-index notation or splitting.
